reason: The done/push/shrink/drop thing is honestly my 11am problem, so I'd sign up for the free plan and maybe try the trial. But I wouldn't pay $12 a month in the first month; I'd sit on the free tier and see if I actually keep using it past week two like every other planner I've tried.
objection: I don't need email and contacts in my planner, so it feels like I'd be paying for a whole suite when I only want the rescheduling part. And I've abandoned enough of these apps that I don't trust myself to stick with it.
would_change_my_mind: If the free plan ran out of what I need right when the habit stuck, or there was a cheaper planner-only tier around $5-6, I'd pay.
